stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria require full requirements elaboration by openspec first. Multi-platform scope (GO, UP, MX) and third-party SDK integration (ContentStack Live Preview) add technical complexity. The explicit limitation around protected pages/content has security implications (unauthorized draft access) and edge cases (dynamic data, partial content states, cross-platform consistency) that speckit must harden. No existing spec or prior hand-curation found in the codebase — this is a greenfield story needing both agents, openspec first then speckit reviews.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — no live_preview config, no preview API route, no context.preview handling, and no livePreviewQuery() usage exist anywhere in the codebase. The Contentstack SDK's live_preview feature requires: (1) live_preview config block on the Stack, (2) a preview API route to receive Contentstack's webhook/polling callbacks, (3) passing preview context through to queries so they return draft content. All queries currently use SSG via getStaticProps with fallback:false, so Next.js Preview Mode must be enabled to serve dynamic draft content. Direct Stack consumers in newsService, getEventsList, and _contentstack_getNewsArticles bypass ContentstackFactory and each need live preview query support.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with detailed notes about the current codebase state. I created all 17 ACs from scratch, informed by reading the actual source files. Key observations from code review: (1) contentstack.ts exports a singleton `Stack` initialized without any `live_preview` config and a `ContentstackFactory` class that wraps it — both need live preview support; (2) [[...slug]].tsx uses getStaticProps with fallback:false and no preview handling; (3) newsService.ts, getEventsList.ts, and _contentstack_getNewsArticles.ts all import `Stack` directly and bypass ContentstackFactory, each constructing queries inline — all three need live preview query support; (4) No live_preview/preview/setPreviewData references exist anywhere. ACs are organized into: config (AC1), preview API route success/failure/validation (AC2-4), draft content rendering (AC5-6), query-path coverage for factory and direct consumers (AC7-10), exit preview (AC11), security/no-leak (AC12), graceful degradation (AC13), SSG regression (AC14), protected pages limitation (AC15), missing-entry edge case (AC16), and multi-codeline consistency (AC17). I flagged AC15 (protected pages) because the story acknowledges this limitation but does not define expected behavior. I also flagged the interactive maps stack (separate Stack instance in contentstack.ts) which may need its own live preview config but is not mentioned in the story.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. Openspec identified the novel capability gap with technical depth: no live_preview config, no preview API route, no context.preview handling, no livePreviewQuery() usage anywhere, and three direct Stack consumers (newsService, getEventsList, _contentstack_getNewsArticles) bypassing ContentstackFactory. Speckit read the actual source files, authored 8 observable verification criteria (all describe what a tester sees on rendered pages, not internal mechanisms), constructed a thorough guardVocabulary blacklist/whitelist, and flagged two real gaps: (1) protected pages behavior is acknowledged but undefined, (2) the interactive maps Stack instance (second contentstack.Stack() call in contentstack.ts) may need its own live_preview config but is not mentioned in the story. The fixSiteAnalysis prescribes 5 specific, actionable fix sites — all 8 declared paths verified to EXIST in the metrolinx codeline. BLOCKING ISSUE: the story title is '[GO, UP, MX]' (multi-codeline), but the perCodeline resolution data shows that 3 of the 5 prescribed fix-site files do not exist in the gotransit or upexpress codelines: src/services/newsService.ts (GO has blogService.ts instead; UP has blogService.ts), src/api/getEventsList.ts (absent in both GO and UP), and src/api/utils/_contentstack_getNewsArticles.ts (GO has contentstack_getBlogArticles.ts; UP has no equivalent). A fourth file, src/components/contentstack/ContentstackAttention/content.mock.ts, is also absent in GO and UP (the directory itself does not exist in either codeline). An implementer following this spec in GO or UP would be directed to edit nonexistent files and every retry would reproduce that failure. The spec is ready for MX implementation alone (~0.85 quality) but is NOT ready as a multi-codeline story. If implementation is intended to be MX-only in this phase with GO/UP deferred, the blocking flag can be downgraded to advisory. Speckit's note about '17 ACs' while only 8 verificationCriteria are shown is the expected brownfield redaction pattern — not a defect, not scored against. The empty acceptanceCriteria array is correct by brownfield policy.

flags.why: The story targets [GO, UP, MX] but 3 of 5 prescribed fixSiteAnalysis files do not exist in gotransit or upexpress: src/services/newsService.ts (GO/UP have blogService.ts instead), src/api/getEventsList.ts (absent in both), src/api/utils/_contentstack_getNewsArticles.ts (GO has contentstack_getBlogArticles.ts; UP has no equivalent). A fourth file, src/components/contentstack/ContentstackAttention/content.mock.ts, is also absent in GO/UP (directory does not exist). All 8 declared paths DO exist in metrolinx. An implementer sent to GO or UP cannot function. If this phase is MX-only, downgrade to advisory.

Speckit itself flagged that the story acknowledges a limitation around protected pages but does not define expected behavior when a draft preview is requested for a protected/restricted page. No verification criterion covers this edge case. A writer can proceed but should clarify expected behavior (e.g., redirect, error, or no draft served).

Speckit identified that contentstack.ts initializes a second Stack instance for interactive maps (using INTERACTIVE_MAPS_STACK_* env vars) which may need its own live_preview config. The fixSiteAnalysis for contentstack.ts mentions adding live_preview to this second Stack call, but no verification criterion covers interactive maps preview behavior. A writer should confirm whether interactive maps are in scope.
